title: Q-LIN: counted quantum score search with linear original copies

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE Q-LIN algorithm and exact parameter rule of proof.md recover all of s from independent ideal source copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including source rejections, discarded copies, numerical-label errors, failed quantum search trials and the acquisition abort, its total charged sequential work T is O(n^6 2^((1/2)n)). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2; the SAME fully specified algorithm at n=1 has finite costs absorbed by absolute outer constants. Its exact envelope growth index is 1. All constants are independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-only tolerance declaration for this same configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE Q-LIN algorithm and exact parameter rule of proof.md recover all of s from independent ideal source copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including source rejections, discarded copies, numerical-label errors, failed quantum search trials and the acquisition abort, its peak classical bits S_C is O(n^2). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2; the SAME fully specified algorithm at n=1 has finite costs absorbed by absolute outer constants. Its exact envelope growth index is 0. All constants are independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-only tolerance declaration for this same configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE Q-LIN algorithm and exact parameter rule of proof.md recover all of s from independent ideal source copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including source rejections, discarded copies, numerical-label errors, failed quantum search trials and the acquisition abort, its peak qubits S_Q is O(n). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2; the SAME fully specified algorithm at n=1 has finite costs absorbed by absolute outer constants. Its exact envelope growth index is 0. All constants are independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-only tolerance declaration for this same configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE Q-LIN algorithm and exact parameter rule of proof.md recover all of s from independent ideal source copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including source rejections, discarded copies, numerical-label errors, failed quantum search trials and the acquisition abort, its total acquired ORIGINAL source copies Q including rejections and discards is O(n). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2; the SAME fully specified algorithm at n=1 has finite costs absorbed by absolute outer constants. Its exact envelope growth index is 0. All constants are independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-only tolerance declaration for this same configuration.

For the same Q-LIN algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
